summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and essential tremor was admitted for acute kidney injury with a creatinine of 4.4, up from her baseline of 1.9. The cause was attributed to volume depletion and medication non-adherence, following an incident where she was found unresponsive at home after missing two days of medications. During her hospitalization, she was treated with IV fluids, medication reconciliation, and discontinuation of nephrotoxic and fall-risk drugs including furosemide and oxybutynin. Her blood pressure was optimized with amlodipine and uptitrated metoprolol. Psychiatric evaluation led to a switch from citalopram to mirtazapine for depression and poor appetite, and nutritional support was enhanced with supplements. Her kidney function improved to a creatinine of 2.7, glycemic control stabilized with reduced insulin dosing, and a safe discharge plan was established with home health aide, occupational therapy, and follow-up for supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. She was discharged home with improved mental status and a comprehensive support plan.
